claims.explanation: SC-9 is a naphthalenesulfonamide PKC activator that acts on PRKCA; its selective antiproliferative effect likely depends on PKC-pathway signaling competence, so lines with high PRKCA/PKC-pathway expression and intact PKC signaling are most sensitive, while loss of PKC components or dependence on counteracting survival pathways confers resistance. The transcriptional response (PRKCH, PLCB3, MYLK, NOTCH1 up) supports a PKC/calcium-linked growth-suppressive program rather than a general cytotoxic effect.

features.basis: SC-9 directly activates PKC-alpha; higher target expression predicts greater growth inhibition (PMID 2398390, 3756133)
PKC-eta is induced in the most responsive virtual-cell line, indicating PKC-pathway engagement
PLC-beta3 upregulation supports DAG/Ca2+ co-activation of PKC required for SC-9 effect
SC-9 activates Ca2+/phospholipid-dependent myosin light chain phosphorylation (PMID 3756133)
Notch1 upregulation in responsive cells suggests growth-arrest/differentiation signaling downstream of PKC
Sestrin-1 induction indicates stress/antioxidant response that may blunt SC-9 cytotoxicity
Proliferation marker down in responsive line; high PCNA reflects proliferative capacity opposing growth inhibition
Constitutive RTK/PI3K signaling can bypass PKC-mediated growth suppression
Loss of PTEN hyperactivates PI3K/AKT survival signaling, counteracting PKC-driven growth arrest
p53 loss reduces stress-induced growth arrest/apoptosis that PKC activation may trigger
Oncogenic KRAS drives MAPK proliferation that can override PKC-mediated inhibition
Loss of p16/CDKN2A releases cell-cycle brakes, reducing sensitivity to PKC-induced arrest
